markets: Sells to property managers worldwide; offices in New York and Tel Aviv, listings on Airbnb, Booking.com and Vrbo.
rationale: B2B software brand with little consumer reach; F1 could serve as customer hospitality, but fit is modest.

name: SAIC Mobility
desc: Chinese ride-hailing and mobility service company backed by state-owned automaker SAIC Motor, running a consumer ride-hailing app.
markets: Consumer ride-hailing app operating in Chinese cities only; no international profile.
rationale: Chinese domestic mobility service with state-owned parent; F1 offers little commercial value for its home-market users.

name: Elan Group
desc: Indian property developer building commercial, retail and residential projects such as Elan Miracle and Elan Town Centre in Delhi NCR.
markets: Projects in the Delhi NCR region only, selling to property buyers and tenants.
rationale: Local property developer with regional brand awareness and no international ambitions; weak F1 fit.

name: Corinthia Hotels
desc: Luxury hotel group operating Corinthia hotels in London, Budapest, Lisbon, Malta, Prague and Doha, with residences and spa.
markets: Hotels in Europe and Doha; part of a Malta-based hotel investment group.
rationale: Luxury hotel brand with London, Budapest and Doha locations in F1 host countries; hospitality fit is plausible but scale is small.

name: Haven Holidays
desc: UK holiday park operator with around 30 coastal parks offering caravan and lodge holidays for families.
markets: Parks on the British coast only, serving UK family holidaymakers.
rationale: Domestic family holiday brand with consumer marketing; F1 audience overlap is limited, so fit is weak.

name: Holidu
desc: Holiday rental search engine founded in 2014, aggregating holiday homes and apartments from partner platforms for travellers.
markets: Sells to travellers searching holiday homes, mainly across Europe; no verified activity in other world regions.
rationale: Consumer travel platform with modest marketing scale; F1 race-weekend rentals are a plausible but not obvious activation.

name: ONroute
desc: Operator of highway service centres along Ontario's 400-series highways, offering fuel, food and retail to travellers.
markets: Sites on Ontario highways only; customers are motorists and travellers.
rationale: Local roadside operator with no international footprint and little marketing culture; weak F1 fit.

name: Cedar Fair
desc: Former US amusement park operator that owned Cedar Point and Knott's Berry Farm, merged into Six Flags in 2024.
markets: Parks in the US and Canada before the 2024 merger; now run by the combined Six Flags company.
rationale: The Cedar Fair business no longer exists as a separate company, so a separate F1 partnership is not possible.
changed: Merged with Six Flags in 2024 to form Six Flags Entertainment Corporation

name: Xenia Hotels & Resorts
desc: US lodging real estate investment trust owning upper-upscale hotels and resorts operated by Marriott, Hyatt, Hilton and other brands.
markets: Owns hotels in US markets only, managed by third-party operators.
rationale: Hotel landlord without a consumer brand, as its hotels are run by third-party operators; weak F1 fit.

name: Archer Hotel Capital
desc: Amsterdam real estate investment company focused on hotels and hospitality property, according to Crunchbase; holdings and scale are not confirmed.
markets: Based in the Netherlands; holdings and customers are not confirmed, so no verified international activity.
rationale: Appears to be an investor rather than a consumer brand; too little information to judge, and F1 fit looks weak.

name: Critical Metals Corp
desc: Mining company developing the Tanbreez rare earths project in Greenland and the Wolfsberg lithium project in Austria.
markets: Projects in Greenland and Austria; no production yet, so buyers of rare earth and lithium materials are future customers.
rationale: Pre-revenue mining developer with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite a possible investor-awareness angle.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq through a SPAC merger in 2024

name: Ella Resorts
desc: Greek resort and tourist accommodation company based in Attica, according to Crunchbase; properties and ownership are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Greece; properties and customers not confirmed, so no verified international activity or expansion plans.
rationale: Too little verified information to judge; likely a modest resort business with weak F1 fit.

name: LY.com (Tongcheng Travel)
desc: Chinese online travel platform where users book flights, trains, hotels and attractions, operated by Tongcheng Travel.
markets: Customers are mainly Chinese domestic travellers; no verified large overseas expansion.
rationale: Large Chinese consumer travel brand with domestic focus; F1 offers limited value for its audience.

name: Yanolja
desc: Korean travel platform with a leading booking app for motels and hotels and software for accommodation operators.
markets: Strong in South Korea, with software and booking activity in other Asian markets; global ambitions are not verified.
rationale: Large Korean consumer travel brand expanding in Asia; F1 audience overlaps modestly, so fit is plausible but not obvious.

name: Mafengwo
desc: Chinese travel community and booking platform where users share travel guides, reviews and itineraries and book hotels and tours.
markets: Customers are mainly Chinese travellers; no verified large overseas operations.
rationale: Chinese consumer travel brand with domestic focus; F1 offers limited value for its audience.

name: Blueground
desc: Provider of furnished apartments for medium- and long-term stays, leasing and managing thousands of units in cities worldwide.
markets: Apartments in cities across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, serving relocating professionals.
rationale: Corporate-housing brand in race cities such as Miami and Dubai; F1 hospitality could suit but marketing scale is modest.

name: TerraPay
desc: Global payments company providing cross-border payments and remittances into mobile wallets, bank accounts and cash points.
markets: Operates across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas, connecting banks, wallets and money-transfer operators.
rationale: B2B payments brand seeking global visibility; F1 offers technology showcase and partner hospitality, though payments rivals Visa and Mastercard dominate.

name: Vinpearl
desc: Vietnamese hotel, resort and leisure brand of Vingroup, operating luxury hotels, resorts, golf courses and the VinWonders theme parks.
markets: Resorts, hotels and parks in Vietnam; customers are mainly Vietnamese and Asian visitors.
rationale: Large Vietnamese hospitality brand with Vingroup backing; F1 could showcase Vietnam tourism, though operations are domestic.

name: Auro Travel
desc: Madrid-based Spanish operator of chauffeur-driven ride-hailing (VTC) services, described as the largest in Spain, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Operates in Spain; no verified international activity or expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic consumer transport service with limited brand scale; F1 offers weak value.

name: Casago
desc: Vacation rental and property management company that runs and markets short-term rental homes for owners in resort destinations.
markets: Managed rental homes in US resort destinations; no verified international activity or expansion plans.
rationale: Regional rental manager with modest brand; F1 race-weekend rentals in US host cities are possible but weak.

name: Oberoi Realty
desc: Indian real estate developer building premium residential, commercial, retail and hospitality projects, mainly in Mumbai.
markets: Projects concentrated in Mumbai; customers are property buyers and tenants.
rationale: Domestic property developer with local brand strength but no international ambitions or marketing need; weak F1 fit.

name: AvantStay
desc: Luxury vacation rental company that operates large, professionally managed homes in destinations such as Lake Tahoe and Scottsdale.
markets: Managed homes in US destinations; no verified international activity or expansion plans.
rationale: Consumer rental brand with a young affluent audience; F1 fits US races in Austin and Miami, but marketing scale is modest.

name: Exoticca
desc: Online travel company selling packaged tours and trips to destinations across Asia, Africa, Latin America and Europe.
markets: Customers mainly in Spain and other European countries buying tours to destinations worldwide; no confirmed activity elsewhere.
rationale: Consumer tour brand with digital marketing focus; F1 offers limited fit beyond race-trip packages.

name: h.wood Group
desc: Hospitality company operating restaurants, nightclubs and lounges such as Delilah, Bootsy Bellows, Poppy and Craig's.
markets: Venues in Los Angeles, Las Vegas, Miami, New York and London serving celebrity and affluent clientele.
rationale: Celebrity-led nightlife brand with venues in F1 host cities including Miami and Las Vegas; fits race-weekend hospitality and events.

name: Hurb
desc: Brazilian online travel agency selling discounted hotel stays, packages, flights and experiences, formerly named Hotel Urbano.
markets: Customers are mainly Brazilian travellers; any operations outside Brazil are not confirmed.
rationale: Consumer travel brand with Brazilian marketing focus; Sao Paulo Grand Prix packages are plausible, but fit is limited.
changed: Renamed from Hotel Urbano to Hurb

name: Wander
desc: Luxury vacation rental company operating high-end homes with smart-home technology, curated amenities and concierge services.
markets: Homes in US destinations; no verified international activity or expansion plans.
rationale: Premium rental brand with technology angle and affluent guests; F1 fit is plausible for Austin, but scale is modest.

name: Kasa Living
desc: Hospitality company operating apartment-hotels, converting apartment buildings and hotels into tech-enabled stays with app-based check-in.
markets: Properties in US cities; no verified international activity or expansion plans.
rationale: Tech-led accommodation brand with modest marketing scale and US-only operations; F1 offers limited value.

name: Limehome
desc: Provider of digital aparthotels, converting vacant commercial spaces into serviced apartments with app-based self check-in.
markets: Aparthotels in Germany and other European countries; no verified activity outside Europe.
rationale: Tech-led accommodation brand with city-centre locations; F1 race-weekend stays are plausible but marketing scale is small.

name: Grande Asset Hotels and Property
desc: Thai hotel owner and operator controlling the Royal Orchid Hotel and Grande Centre Point hotel brands.
markets: Hotels in Bangkok and other Thai locations; customers are mainly business and leisure travellers.
rationale: Thai hotel group with domestic focus and small marketing scale; weak F1 fit.

name: Royal Orchid Hotel
desc: Hotel company behind the Royal Orchid Sheraton on Bangkok's Chao Phraya river, owned by Grande Asset Hotels and Property.
markets: One Bangkok hotel serving business and leisure guests; no operations outside Thailand.
rationale: Single-hotel owner with only local awareness and no marketing scale; weak F1 fit.

name: Korean Air
desc: South Korea's flag carrier, flying passengers and cargo from Incheon to about 100 cities worldwide.
markets: Flies across Asia, North America, Europe and Oceania from its Incheon hub; acquired Asiana Airlines in 2024.
rationale: Brand-led global airline; rivals Qatar Airways, Singapore Airlines and Etihad already partner F1, and Asian audience and hospitality fit well.
changed: Completed acquisition of Asiana Airlines in December 2024

name: Alandalus Property
desc: Saudi real estate company that owns and operates commercial properties, including Andalus Mall in Jeddah.
markets: Properties in Saudi Arabia only; customers are retail tenants and shoppers.
rationale: Domestic Saudi property owner with a Jeddah mall near the Saudi Grand Prix; limited marketing scale makes the fit weak.

name: SALTO Systems
desc: Spanish maker of electronic access control and smart locks serving hotels, offices, universities and hospitals.
markets: Sells locks and software in over 100 countries across Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B smart-lock maker with hospitality customers; F1 offers hotel-industry networking and technology showcase, though awareness is B2B.

name: YY Group Holding
desc: Singapore-based live streaming agency and hospitality-freelance services company working with hosts and talent on platforms such as BIGO Live.
markets: Works with hosts and talent in Asia on streaming platforms and provides freelance staffing services.
rationale: Small B2B creator-economy company with low brand awareness and limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Club Med
desc: French all-inclusive holiday resort operator founded in 1950, known for beach and ski resorts with sports and family activities.
markets: Resorts in dozens of countries across Europe, Asia, the Americas and Africa, selling to guests worldwide.
rationale: Premium holiday brand with international affluent guests; F1 hospitality and sports positioning fit, though it has no current link.
changed: Acquired by Fosun in 2015
